item.title: Giants worked out LB Kenneth Murray, 17 others, on Monday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Giants worked out 18 players on Monday, including veteran linebacker Kenneth Murray.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants worked out 18 players on Monday, including veteran linebacker Kenneth Murray.

They are expected to sign former Iowa State tight end Tyler Moore, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports. Moore is an undrafted free agent who tried out with the Panthers in the spring.

Offensive tackle Jake Curhan, defensive tackle Marlon Davidson, tight end Zach Davidson, defensive tackle Daniel Ekuale, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi, offensive tackle Luke Felix-Fualalo, defensive back Tony Grimes, quarterback Jake Haener, wide receiver Malik Heath, running back Kylin James, linebacker Chandler Martin, wide receiver Eric McAlister, defensive back Ahmaad Moses, offensive tackle Derek Simmons, tight end Scotty Washington and defensive back Sam Webb also worked out for the Giants.

Murray, 27, spent last season in Dallas after the Cowboys traded with the Titans for him. He started 16 games and finished second on the team in tackles with 81 behind rookie fifth-round pick Shemar James, who had 91. Murray also added four tackles for loss, two pass breakups, a sack and a fumble recovery.

He has remained a free agent since March.

item.title: Chiefs' second-round rookie R Mason Thomas says Chiefs hid their interest in drafting him
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Chiefs were targeting former Oklahoma defensive end R Mason Thomas as a high priority with their second-round draft pick, and they didn't want anyone to know.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs were targeting former Oklahoma defensive end R Mason Thomas as a high priority with their second-round draft pick, and they didn't want anyone to know. Including Thomas.

Thomas, who went to Kansas City with the 40th overall pick in April, says he was shocked when his phone rang during the second round and it was the Chiefs, talking to him for the first time since a meeting at the Scouting Combine two months earlier.

"I would've never known a Kansas City, Missouri, area code would call my phone on draft day. They didn't really talk as much," Thomas said. "I had a formal meeting with them, and that was the first meeting of the Combine. After that we didn't talk. So I guess they're low-key. They like to keep it quiet."

Some teams like to bring in the players they're interested in drafting for meetings at the team facility to get to know them better. Other teams view those meetings as a way for other teams to identify the players they want and perhaps move up ahead of them in the draft. The Chiefs decided not to let anyone know Thomas was their guy, until they let Thomas know when they were on the clock.
